newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea cash Brent crude moves into backwardation.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea cash Brent crude moves into backwardation.

text.p: The front end of the North Sea Brent paper curve headed into backwardation on Friday, although some traders questioned whether the market's more bullish tone was reflected in the wet crude market.
A June/July spread traded early on Friday at +3 cents, up from deals at -3 cents on the U.S. aftermarket.
July/August also moved higher, but was still assessed slightly in contango at -5/-1 cents.
CFDs for next week (May 12-16) were assessed firmer at July Brent -12/-7, a 5 cent premium to the following week (May 19-23).
June Brent was 12 cents higher at $18.81 a barrel on the IPE screen at 1058 GMT in a follow-through to Thursday's heavy gains of over 50 cents in a U.S.-led technical rally.
The wet Brent market was murky with no firm Brent paper-related bids and offers seen in the market after recent deals were done on a quotes-related basis.
Some traders said that unsold May barrels may keep the lid on Dated Brent values and differentials for other grades.
"The sentiment is getting more bullish, but it's a bit of a schizophrenic market considering that the programmes are out next week and there are still reasonably good avails," said one.
Wet Brent was notionally assessed around June Brent -20 cents, eight cents up from the last paper-related deal.
Four Brent cargoes loading May 24-28 were seen nominated from the paper chains on Friday.
Thursday's leap in Brent paper values helped widen Brent/Dubai spreads which had been squeezed sharply this week.
July Brent/Dubai was assessed some 10-20 cents wider than midweek at +98 cents/$1.02, while July/August, which traded late on Thursday at $1.09 was pegged at $1.12/$1.18.
Dubai intermonth spreads held on to gains, with June/July at +35/+50 cents and July/August at +13/+18 cents.
